newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ivory Coast debt relief terms near finalisation.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast debt relief terms near finalisation.

text.p: The restructuring of Ivory Coast's debt to banks and financial institutions is nearly complete, the Ivory Coasts' finance ministry said in a statement released in Paris on Friday.

The outstanding debt after restructuring will be divided equally into French francs and U.S. dollars, the statement said. Thirty percent of the outstanding principal will be repurchased at a price of 24 percent with the cancellation of interest.

Ivory Coast will then exchange with its creditors more than 90 percent of the remaining principal against 20-year reduced interest rate certificates repayable in 21 six-month intervals after 9.5 years of grace.

The rest will be exchanged against 30-year, 50 percent discount certificates with their total reimbursement, upon their expiry, guaranteed by zero-coupon bonds of an equivalent maturity. Interest arrears, sharply reduced, will be exchanged against certificates of interest arrears with a maturity of 20 years.
The ministry's statement said the operation would be a great success for Ivory Coast because it would result in a sharp reduction of its bank debt in stock and future service.
Ivory Coast's debt is about $23 billion including interest arrears, or 250 percent of gross national product.
